Party Grocery List

Hosting is mostly about not running out. This party grocery list covers the food, drinks, and supplies a get-together needs, with rough per-guest amounts so you can scale it to your headcount. Confirm your guest count and any allergies first, then adjust the quantities up or down. See more grocery and shopping lists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Party Grocery List · 21 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    A mix of soft drinks, juice, and sparkling water

    Plan about 2-3 drinks per guest for the first few hours.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Beer, wine, or a batch cocktail, if you're serving alcohol
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plenty of ice — more than you think you'll need

    Roughly 1-2 lbs (0.5-1 kg) per guest for drinks and coolers.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Coffee, tea, and milk for later in the night
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A main or two — a platter, tray bake, pizzas, or something on the grill
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Buns, bread, or wraps if you're serving anything handheld
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A couple of dips — hummus, salsa, guacamole, or a cheese dip
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Chips, crackers, pretzels, and nuts for grazing

    Set snacks out before guests arrive to cover the early lull.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    A cheese and charcuterie board — cheeses, cured meats, and crackers
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A veggie platter and fruit for lighter and dietary options

    Always include a vegetarian and a non-alcoholic option.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Dessert — a cake, cookies, or something easy to serve
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Condiments: ketchup, mustard, mayo, and any sauces your mains need
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Paper plates, napkins, cups, and cutlery

    Buy about 1.5x your guest count — plates and cups get swapped.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Serving bowls, platters, and a couple of serving spoons
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Trash bags and a recycling bag, set out where guests can see them
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Paper towels and cleaning wipes for spills
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A cooler or two, plus bags of ice to fill them
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bottle opener, corkscrew, and a can opener
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Aluminum foil, cling film, and containers for leftovers
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Candles, a lighter, and music or a speaker for atmosphere
  • check_box_outline_blank
    A few extras for allergies or kids — a gluten-free snack and a juice option

    Ask guests about allergies when they RSVP.

Frequently asked questions

How much food and drink do I need per person for a party? expand_more

As a rough guide, plan 2-3 drinks per guest for the first couple of hours and around 6-8 appetizer-sized bites each if food is the main event. For ice, allow 1-2 lbs (0.5-1 kg) per person. Always round up a little, and include non-alcoholic drinks and a vegetarian option.

What food is easiest to serve at a party? expand_more

Grazing food is the easiest to host with — dips, chips, a cheese and charcuterie board, veggie platters, and anything guests can serve themselves. Trays that bake in one go, or handheld items like sliders and pizza, save you from plating individual meals and let you enjoy the party too.

What supplies do people forget to buy for a party? expand_more

The commonly forgotten items are ice, extra trash and recycling bags, enough napkins and cups, and serving spoons for shared dishes. A bottle opener and corkscrew, foil and containers for leftovers, and a non-alcoholic plus allergy-friendly option round out what tends to get missed.
